THIS CRL.P IS FILED U/S 482 CR.PC BY THE ADVOCATE FOR THE PETITIONER PRAYING TO QUASH THE FIR IN CR.NO.321/2022 AND THE CHARGE SHEET IN C.C.NO.128/2023 OF BYADARAHALLI POLICE STATION, FOR THE OFFENCE P/U/S 498A, 323, 504, 506 R/W 34 OF IPC AND 3 AND 4 OF D.P. ACT, PENDING ON THE FILE OF CJM RURAL COURT AT BANGALORE RURAL DISTRICT AS AGAINST PETITIONER NO.1 TO 3.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR REPORTING SETTLEMENT, THIS DAY, ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI  ORAL ORDER Petitioner/Accused No.1 and both learned counsel are present.

under Section 482 of Cr.P.C, to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them in C.C.No.128/2023, NC: 2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR (arising out of crime No.321/2022 of Byadarahalli PS) for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504 and 506 r/w Section 34 of I.P.C and Sections 3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.

3. It is submitted by the both learned counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.1 that the dispute between the parties has been settled before the Mediation and memorandum of settlement under Section 89 of CPC r/w Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules,
2005 is filed in M.C.No.8053/2023.

A memo along with certified copy of the order sheet, Mediation settlement agreement, decree in M.C.No.8053/2023 passed on by V Additional Principal Judge,
Family Court, Bengaluru are produced.

sentences.text: As per the Sl.No.10 of the said settlement, respondent No.1 has agreed settle the matter in CC No.128/2023 in respect of which the present petition is filed.
Learned counsel for respondent No.1 herein also admit the said facts.
NC: 2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR 5.

The terms and conditions of settlement arrived at between the parties reads as under:
" MEMORANDUM OF SETTLEMENT UNDER SECTION 89 OF CPC READ WITH RULES 24 AND 25 OF THE KARNATAKA CIVIL PROCEDURE (MEDIATION)
RULES, 2005.
1.
The Petitioner has filed this petition against the Respondent under Section 13 (1) of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for dissolution of his marriage with the respondent/wife.
II. The aforesaid petition was referred to mediation for resolving the dispute between the parties.

During the course of mediation the parties along with their respective advocates were present and they have resolved their dispute and have agreed to the following terms and conditions:
1.
The petitioner and the respondent are Hindus by religion.

Their marriage was solemnized on 02.12.2018 at Parvathamma Ramaiah Mangala Bhavana,
No.1051/153, 7th Block, 60 Feet Road, Next to Mallathahalli R.T.O Office,
Muddinapalya, Bengaluru as per Hindu rites and customs.

2. The parties state and admit that due to irreconcilable differences and incompatibility of temperaments, they are living separately since NC:
2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR 15.02.2020.
The efforts made by the elders, friends and well wishers to resolve the differences between the parties did not yield any fruits.
There is absolutely no chance of a reunion between them.
The petitioner and the respondent know that their marriage is irretrievably broken down and there are no chances of reunion to lead a happy married life.
Hence, the petitioner and the respondent have decided to get the marriage dissolved by a decree of divorce.

3. Both the parties state that they have a male child by name Shivin Sai, born on 03.08.2020 who is presently under the care and custody of the respondent/mother and shall continue to be so in future and the respondent/mother shall be sole authority for submitting applications for VISA, Passport, School-College admissions in future for which the petitioner/father has no objection.
The petitioner/father has voluntarily given up his visitation rights over the minor son and he has no objection to his son to move abroad.

sentences.text: The petitioner has agreed to pay a sum of Rs.12,00,000/-(Rupees Twelve Lakhs Only) to the respondent towards education and welfare of the minor child by way of demand draft NC: 2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR bearing No.049204 dated 03.07.2025 drawn on State Bank of India, Chikkaballapura Branch in favour of the minor son Shivin Sai (Aaadhar No.590009641776)
and the same will be handover to the respondent before the Hon'ble Court at the time of reporting settlement.

5. The respondent/mother undertakes to bear entire expenses including education,
medical and day to day upbringing expenses of the minor son in future.

6. Both parties state and agree that they have no claims of maintenance/permanent alimony against each other either past, present or in future, as both of them are capable of maintaining themselves independently.
7. The parties herein state that they have no claims over movable or immovable properties belonging to each other either existing or to be acquired or inherited at a later stage.

8. The petitioner has agreed to give 40gms of gold chain to the respondent before this Hon'ble Court as such they have no further claims in this regard.
9.
The parties admit and agree that they have no further claims of whatsoever manner NC: 2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR against each other either past, present or future to assist.

10. In view of the settlement arrived to between the parties that the respondent has agreed to assist in closing/quashing C.C.No.128/2023 filed under section 498A, 323,
504, 506 R/w Section 34 of IPC and section 3 & 4 of D.P.Act against the petitioner and his family members pending before Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District.

entities.text: Chief Judicial Magistrate, Bengaluru Rural District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Both parties have agreed to co-operate in allowing the Crl.P.No.11765/2023 filed by the petitioner seeking for quashing of the proceedings in C.C.No.128/2023 pending before the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru.

11. The respondent has also agreed to withdraw Crl.Misc No.783/2024 filed under section 144 of BNSS for maintenance against the respondent pending on the file of V-Addl. Family Court,
Bengaluru.
12. Both the parties state that without pressing on the allegations levelled against each other either orally or expressly arrived at this agreement.

13. The parties admit and agree that there is no collusion or force, fraud or any undue NC:
2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR influence in filing the above petition and entering into this compromise Chethankumar R vs Smt Chaitra J on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/97865972/
4 in the aforesaid manner.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 14. Both the parties admit that they shall not interfere in the lives of each other in future.

III. In view of the aforesaid agreement entered into between the parties, the parties pray that this Hon'ble Court be pleased to dissolve the marriage solemnized on 02.12.2018 at Parvathamma Ramaiah Mangala Bhavana, No.1051/153, 7th Block, 60 Feet Road, Next to Mallathahalli R.T.O Office, Muddinapalya,
Bengaluru by granting a decree of divorce in terms of this agreement.
IV. Parties will appear on 14.07.2025 before the Hon'ble Court for passing of orders in terms of the agreement.

6. Having regard to the fact that the parties have settled their dispute and learned counsel for respondent No.1 also submitted no objections to allow the petition, the petition deserves to be allowed and criminal proceedings pending against them are required to be quashed and accordingly the following:
NC: 2025:KHC:34415 HC-KAR ORDER (i) The petition filed by petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 3 under Section 482 Cr.P.C, is allowed.
(ii) The entire criminal proceedings in C.C.No.128/2023 (Crime No.321/2022 of Byadarahalli PS) on the file of Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru, is hereby quashed.
(iii) The Registry is directed to send copy of this order to the trial Court forthwith.
